outcome_intro: Ask which client devices go out of warranty this quarter and get the list, per client. Device Warranty plus your AI agent looks up Dell, Lenovo and Apple serials with whichever vendor credentials you have, keeps every answer in a local warranty mirror, and answers fleet questions offline: what expires soon, what to refresh next year, and which devices were never verified.

instead_of_say.instead: Paste service tags one at a time into Dell's and Lenovo's warranty pages, then copy each end date into a spreadsheet per client
instead_of_say.say: Look up warranty for every device in this export for Acme Dental

instead_of_say.instead: Sort that spreadsheet by end date before every QBR to find the devices about to lose coverage
instead_of_say.say: Which client devices are out of warranty or expire in the next 90 days?

instead_of_say.instead: Guess next year's hardware refresh from purchase dates someone typed into the PSA
instead_of_say.say: How many devices per client lose coverage in each of the next four quarters?

pain_points: Dell's own community has asked for years for a way to check many service tags at once ("Is there an easy way to enter multiple service tags to check the warranty status on all of my hardware?", Dell Community, May 2022; one reply had over 1,000 computers to check). The accepted answer is a TechDirect API key and scripts.
Warranty end dates live in three vendor portals with three different credentials, so a per-client view means exports, copy and paste, and a spreadsheet that is stale by the next QBR.
Devices nobody could verify (wrong serial, vendor not configured, never checked) silently drop out of the report, so a client finds out their server is out of warranty when it fails.

different_vs_wrappers: This skill keeps every lookup in a local warranty mirror per client, so fleet questions (what expires this quarter, what to refresh next year, what was never verified) are one offline query instead of one vendor call per serial. A wrapper that forwards each question to a vendor API answers one serial at a time and knows nothing about which client owns it.
different_vs_vendor: Dell TechDirect, Lenovo eSupport and Apple Business stay the source of truth for each serial; this skill puts all three behind one command, remembers the answers per client, and answers the cross-client questions none of the portals can.

faqs.a: Yes, on paid ChatGPT plans. ChatGPT connects to remote MCP servers over HTTPS, so it needs the Device Warranty MCP server's token-protected HTTP mode hosted over HTTPS. Step-by-step in the install guide.

faqs.q: Do I need to know how to code?
faqs.a: No. Paste one sentence into Claude Code or Codex and your agent does the install, or run a one-line installer. You enter your credentials once.

faqs.q: Is my client device data safe?
faqs.a: Your data stays on your machine. The CLI, MCP server, and the local mirror are all local. The AI sees query results, not raw bulk data, and credentials are never bundled or transmitted by MSP Skills.
Free. Apache-2.0 licensed. You pay only for whichever AI agent you already use.

faqs.q: Do I need credentials for all three vendors?
faqs.a: No. Every vendor is optional. Dell needs a TechDirect Warranty API client ID and secret, Lenovo a ClientID token from your Lenovo account manager, Apple an Apple Business API account in the client's organization. A vendor without credentials is reported as vendor_unconfigured and never called, and the others keep working. warranty-cli doctor --json lists what each vendor still needs.

faqs.q: Where do the serials come from?
faqs.a: Any CSV or JSON device export with a serial column (manufacturer, model and hostname are optional), for example from your RMM. warranty-cli import devices.csv --customer "Acme Dental" loads it into the mirror; apple-pull loads a client's Apple devices straight from Apple Business.

faqs.q: Will this hit the vendors' rate limits?
faqs.a: It is built to stay inside them: Dell lookups go 100 service tags per call, Lenovo 25 serials per call spaced 250 ms apart, Apple one serial per call. recheck refreshes only stale or soon-expiring devices, and --max-calls caps a run.

governance_summary: The skill reads warranty and coverage data from Dell, Lenovo and Apple and changes nothing at any vendor. It writes only its own local warranty mirror (import, lookup, recheck, apple-pull), which you can preview with --dry-run, and over MCP those saves need confirm. Let an agent read and report freely; keep a human on credential commands and on local-data purge.
